preamble: A voiceless [ts] from /d/ is rare. It arises in two steps: assibilation of /d/ to [dz] next to a front vowel or yod, then devoicing. Belarusian shows it with dzekanne plus final devoicing: soft /dʲ/ is pronounced [dzʲ], and at the end of a word this becomes [tsʲ] (медзь [mʲetsʲ] 'copper'). In Italian, Latin -dj- usually gives voiced [ddz], but some words have a voiceless variant (pranzo [ˈprantso] < prandium).

examples.note: The medial /dʲ/ stays voiced [dzʲ]; the final one devoices to [tsʲ].
Latin -dj- gave an affricate; the voiceless variant is recorded alongside voiced /dz/.

sources: Wikipedia contributors. Belarusian phonology (Tsyekannye and dzyekannye). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarusian_phonology
